decision: Footage search: no handheld-scanner footage exists in the Sera dump (all ~130 FX30 clips sheeted June 23-July 6; Dropbox search 'Sera' finds only this folder + a posted short). Stock-part removal exists: 4351 (stock front bumper lifted off, hood open), 4358/4359 (rear bumper pulled away at the corner, never fully off).
why: Brief asked for crew scanning with the handheld scanner; inventing it is not possible. The removal beat uses the real front-bumper lift-off; the missing scanner beat is flagged in review.md for the user.

decision: Music starts at 7.825 s of the Sera track (beat 13 of a 100.0 BPM kick grid, t0=0.0254); video ends with the music at 30.6 s
why: Track has no quiet intro; band-novelty shows phrase changes every 16 beats (9.625 s, 19.225 s). Offsetting puts the first phrase change at 1.80 s (hook: 1:1 cut within 2 s) and the second at 11.40 s for the front-bumper 1:1 cut; kick-anchored grid per lessons.

decision: FX30 S-Log3/S-Gamut3.Cine graded with a generated LUT (tools/slog3_lut.py: legal-range decode, Sony S-Log3 inverse, SGamut3.Cine->709 matrix, Hable shoulder, 709 OETF); 16:9 4K cropped to 9:16 windows per clip
why: ive tonemap only handles iPhone HLG; ungraded S-Log3 is washed out next to the scan renders

decision: Opening 1:1 cut: 4342 frame 433 (18.060 s), 9:16 window x0=2160 y0=498 zoom 1.3 over the car's front right half; full-car scan; camera solved in the full 4K frame (7 landmarks, RMSE 6.9 px at 3840 wide) then converted to the crop with Blender lens shift (tools/crop_cam.py)
why: A 9:16 window cannot hold the whole car (front = 1820 px of 3840); cropping into the car keeps bumper->mirror depth for the solve and hides most of the raised rear hatch (not a scanned state). Onion check: headlight, hood edge, fog lamp, fender and mirror line up within a few px

decision: Focal left free (20.6 mm solved) instead of fixing 24 mm
why: XML sidecars name the lens (FE 24-70 GM II) but record no focal; a 24 mm lock doubled RMSE (14.6 vs 6.9 px) - likely uncorrected wide-end barrel distortion; the crop onion is what matters and it aligns

decision: Verified inside surfaces: front bumper scan (1,800,000 tris) and rear-bumper-only scan (4,999,998 tris) both show the inner ribs/tabs/plate recess when rendered from behind (match/bumpers_inside_check.jpg) -> INSIDE + OUTSIDE may be claimed for both bumpers
why: Lessons: render the hidden side before putting the claim on screen

decision: Front 1:1 cut uses the 'Hood open' state scan (bumper off + hood up, 5,000,000 tris) over the full car trimmed at u=0.82 m (tools/composite.py); x-ray base = full car + 'front bumper removed' fascia (u>1.33 m, hood closed) + 'Rear Bumper Removed' (u<-0.88 m)
why: 4351 at the cut shows bumper off with the hood propped open - the 'front bumper removed' scan has the hood closed, 'Hood open' matches the state exactly. For the x-ray the hood-closed state reads better and its own hood had a coverage hole, so the hood comes from the full car

decision: Front 1:1 cut: 4351 frame 250 (10.427 s, sharpest frame after the lift - the following frames are pan-blurred), crop x0=0 zoom 1.2, scan compA (full car + Hood open state). Camera: hand-placed look-at at bay height then 2D similarity nudge (focal 23.4 mm, lens shift) verified by onion (match/check_front.jpg): fan, headlight, cross-bar, hood edge within ~20 px at 1080 wide
why: Landmark PnP failed (25 px at every focal) on the blurred, half-occluded frame; an automatic gradient-correlation refiner (tools/grad_refine.py) 'improved' its score by rolling 14 deg and dropping the camera to 0.34 m - degenerate, rejected. Onion is the ground truth (CLAUDE.md)

decision: Timeline (100 BPM kick grid, beat 0.6 s, music from track 7.825 s): IRL open 0-1.8 | 1:1 scan 1.8-4.2 | IRL rear-bumper pull 4.2-6.0 | rear bumper explode 6.0-9.0 | IRL front-bumper lift 9.0-11.4 | 1:1 bay hold 11.4-12.6 | front bumper explode 12.6-15.6 | x-ray reassembly 15.6-20.4 | dissolve to listing 20.4-27.0
why: Holds of 3/4/3/5/4/2/5/8 beats (lessons: vary holds, cut on accents); 1:1 cuts land on the two 16-beat phrase changes (1.8 s, 11.4 s); ends with the listing's WebZoom, music faded at 27.0 s like the 240SX reel's length

decision: Rear section uses real crew pulling the rear bumper corner (4359 16.4-18.3 s) then a hard (non-1:1) cut to the rear-bumper-removed composite with the rear bumper scan dropping below and spinning about Z
why: The real rear bumper never fully comes off on camera, so no part-state frame exists to solve a 1:1 cut against; stacking the part below the car keeps it clear of the body/lens in 9:16 (lessons)

decision: Front 1:1 shot holds the matched bay for 2 beats, then cuts on the accent to a wide front 3/4 where the front bumper rises above the nose and spins
why: The matched crop camera is effectively a 14 deg telephoto - a 1.6 m bumper cannot be shown inside it, and pulling back with the large lens shift drifts the car out of frame (previewed)

decision: X-ray reassembly: base = full car + front-bumper-removed fascia + Rear Bumper Removed; both bumper scans translate into place (no rotation); 40 deg orbit about (0,0,0.7) ending exactly on the listing hero camera (silhouette IoU 0.865 vs the hero render), morph to clay/listing background over the last 20 %
why: 240SX v4 rules: x-ray, translate only, end on the listing's angle and dissolve so it reads as one object

decision: X-ray base switched to the full car with bumper surfaces cut away (tools/trim_by_parts.py, triangles within 12 mm of either bumper scan); clay tuned to 0.05 (car median 140 vs listing 138), background to listing grey
why: First final used the 'Rear Bumper Removed' state scan, which was captured with the hatch open and tail lights out - the end frame read as a broken car and did not match the closed car in the listing hero

decision: Triangle counter (14,999,999) moved from the opening scan shot to the x-ray shot (15.8-19.2 s)
why: On the 1:1 shot the silver car fills the whole 9:16 frame, so off-white HUD text had no dark background and was unreadable (checked frame 2.6 s); x-ray is on black

decision: HUD counter replaced by a static label '14,999,999 TRIANGLES / FULL CAR SCAN'
why: ScanHUD's Counter uses Easing.out(Easing.exp), which ends at 1-2^-10: it displays 14,985,351, not the header value - an invented number on screen. remotion/ is outside this project's scope; reported to the user

decision: v2: both 1:1 IRL crops widened to the full sensor height (zoom 1.0): opening window x0=1640 centred on the car's front (was zoom 1.3 on its right half), front lift x0=0 (was zoom 1.2); crop cameras re-derived from the same full-frame solves (tools/crop_cam.py), onions re-checked (qa onion_v2)
why: User: 'the irl to cgi crops from the video are awfully close'. Zoom 1.0 is the widest full-bleed 9:16 window of a 16:9 4K frame; the front lift frame cannot go wider (camera ~2 m from the car)

decision: v3 order: front (IRL open, 1:1 full car, IRL front lift, 1:1 bay, front bumper off, behind the bumper) -> side (butterfly doors) -> rear (IRL rear pull, rear bumper off, behind it) -> x-ray -> listing; v2's rear-before-front block removed
why: All-reels brief + addendum B: travel front->side->rear, each section in one continuous sequence; direction.md section-coverage table

decision: Bumper beats split into two shots cut on a kick: (1) whole nose/tail in frame, bumper drops below into black and turns ~170 deg about vertical to face its scanned inside to the lens; (2) close 3/4 on the exposed structure from the bumper-removed state with a readable hold
why: Addendum C (bumper-removed data is the hero beat, move in on what's behind it). scan_render supports one camera move per shot, so 'part off then move in' becomes two shots; parts stacked below the car keep clear of the body and the frame edges in 9:16 (previewed 3 iterations: forward/toward-lens paths clipped)

decision: Doors shot uses the 'Door Open' capture as captured (both doors up), composited onto the full car only inside the door zone (tools/doors_comp.py: full-car triangles in the zone with no captured geometry within 15 mm = closed doors/glass are dropped); no opening animation
why: Addendum D: show an open state only from its scan, never fake an opening; the capture is cabin-only so the full car supplies the nose and tail

decision: Cut from v2: s3_rear, s6_frontx (too wide, spun across the body), v2 x-ray timing, 2.3 s of dead end card (WebZoom 6.6 -> 3.6 s, zoom 48 frames)

decision: Spoiler removed / front bumper removed (hood closed) / Hood Open Bumper in scans not shown

decision: Two new shots: designed front bumper rises onto the bumper-less scan right after 'behind the front bumper' (11.4 phrase change), designed rear bumper after 'behind the rear bumper'; labels NEW FRONT/REAR BUMPER - DESIGNED ON THE SCAN DATA

decision: Finished car = two shots from the posted short 'Toyota Sera at home' (3.79-4.89 s front, 6.09-7.23 s rear), cropped to the lower 70 % (756x1344 window, 1.43x upscale) to remove the burned-in caption; hard cuts on kicks at 23.4 / 24.6, then cut to the listing card at 25.8
why: User: then cut to pictures/videos of the finished car. Only finished-car footage found (Dropbox search; the July 6 FX30 clips are the mould shop, June 28 is the printed test fit). CLAUDE.md: no text over IRL -> the caption had to be cropped out

decision: cam_fin solved by hand (tools/fin_cam.py + onion): level camera 23 deg off the nose toward car-left, 7.5 m, 42 mm on 14.175 mm sensor with lens shift for the 756x1344 crop; bumper/wheels/windshield within ~15 px at 540 w, door tips differ

decision: v5 delivered: sera_scan_process_v5.mp4 (29.97 s)

decision: v7: scan -> finished-car 1:1 changed from a hard cut to a 0.4 s crossfade (24.4-24.8, centred on the 24.6 beat) with both sides held on the matched frame; kit_final 1.6 s (src_fps 75/4), fin_front plays 1.0 s after the fade
why: User: 'crossfade the 1:1 shot'. This is the scan -> real reveal, not the IRL -> scan transformation, so the hard-cut rule does not apply; the two IRL -> scan cuts at 1.8 and 6.0 stay hard. Held frames so the handheld real clip does not drift against the scan during the fade

decision: v8: final match camera re-solved at full resolution (tools/fin_fit.py): 23 deg, 7.5 m, 36.3 mm on 20.25 mm sensor, shift -0.0224/0.084; kit_final re-rendered
why: User: 'match the photo to the transition better in the model'. A 1000 px close-up showed the scan ~18 % too large at the fade - the 540 px onion had hidden it and I had blamed the doors. After the fix body, bumper, wheels and both doors sit within a few px

decision: v9 music: GT2 'What License Test Will You Go With' from 35.364 s; whole edit re-timed to its 8-beat phrases (3.335 s) and half-phrases (50 frames): 1:1 open on the 37.03 fill, drums drop on the bumper lift, crossfade to the finished car mid-phrase, end card on the 63.71 phrase start
why: User supplied the track ('use this music instead'). Analysed: 143.9 BPM, each 2-bar phrase opens with a kick+stab; the intro is sparse, so the reel uses 35-67 s where the drums enter after a fill - gives a hook, a drop and a natural out

decision: v9 punchline: title 'WHAT COULD I DO WITH THIS SCAN?' over the first scan shot (now 3.33 s, re-rendered), answered by the rest of the reel and the 'SCAN DATA NOW AVAILABLE' card
why: User asked for a punchline 'something like what could i do with this scan'. Placed over the scan (never over real footage), in the black above the nose, during the fill before the drop so it reads as the question the reel answers
